finding: README states that there are eight chapter folders, while main.tex and the pinned tree contain nine.

Third-party paper figure has no file-level reuse license in the repository.
Template is stale (2015) and misnames CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported as a United States license.
Upstream image description says 'An ear is show'; excluded visual is replaced by a rights-safe textual substitute.

The static PDF boundary now has a pinned toolchain record, fixed source epoch, and two-pass byte identity; R figure regeneration remains non-hermetic because Rscript, a dependency lock, and a global regeneration driver are absent.
A lone opening brace before the eocesol macro leaves the document inside an unclosed simple group and causes current LaTeX begin-document hooks to fail.
Generated example, guided-practice, exercise, chapter, appendix, figure, table, bibliography, index, and running-head labels otherwise remained English around translated content.
The deterministic PDF declares /Lang id-ID and has reader metadata but is untagged and has no StructTreeRoot; a final accessible surface remains required before corpus completion.

The whole-book working build reports 402 overfull hbox, 1 overfull vbox, and 151 underfull hbox warnings. Every changed and transition page in R011-B001 was rendered and showed no clipping or overlap; later whole-reader QA must re-evaluate the complete translated corpus.

The public answer describes PM10 as particulate matter less than 10 micrograms per cubic meter, conflating the aerodynamic particle-size threshold (10 micrometers) with concentration units (micrograms per cubic meter). The derivative states both quantities separately.
The public answer lists four variables but omits the randomized instruction-group variable needed to describe the experiment. The derivative lists all five variables.

The public answer identifies the explanatory variable as acupuncture versus no acupuncture, but both randomized groups receive acupuncture; the intended contrast is migraine-targeted acupuncture versus placebo acupuncture at non-acupuncture points.
A migraine exercise is indexed under data!stroke. The derivative preserves exercise identity while routing the visible index entry to migraine.

The bundled Census cartographic-boundary metadata requires source acknowledgment, but the exercise text omits it. The derivative adds visible U.S. Census Bureau acknowledgment in prose and in the regenerated figure.

Exercises contain deterministic prose defects: duplicated 'either' in 1.8, 'countries al start' in the 1.12 figure description, and two malformed closing LaTeX quotation marks in 1.10. Natural Indonesian translation carries the intended text only.

The source presents randomized experiments as the only basis for causal inference. The derivative retains their privileged evidential role while noting that nonrandomized studies can support causal inference only under explicit additional assumptions and methods.

The translated Section 1.2 initially rendered an English generated page-reference phrase ('on page 12'). The derivative now localizes the varioref phrase hooks in the source preamble; labels, targets, and page numbers remain unchanged.
The simple-random-sample definition contains the malformed phrase 'and which is equivalent'. The Indonesian B003 body carries the intended definition without the extraneous conjunction.
The nonresponse figure caption says 'surveys studies'. The Indonesian B003 caption expresses the intended subject as survey studies without duplicating the noun.

The accessibility description says the cluster figure contains eight clusters and five highlighted points per selected cluster, while the producer and rendered figure contain nine clusters and six highlighted points. The derivative description now matches the live figure and uses the correct plural.

The malaria example selects villages and then people within each selected village, correctly defining multistage sampling, but its concluding sentence calls the resulting design a cluster sample. The derivative calls it a multistage sample.

The public answer contains two deterministic grammar defects: 'responds his sample' and 'a similar issues'. The Indonesian answer carries the intended nonresponse and convenience-sampling analysis without those defects.

The adjacent rights note identifies David M. Diez as photographer and licenses the image under the textbook's CC BY-SA terms, but the source figure has no visible creator/license credit. B003 adds visible David M. Diez and CC BY-SA 3.0 credit.

The exercise reproduces a quotation from an APA-published article whose expression is not part of the textbook's reusable CC BY-SA rights closure. B003 excludes the quotation and retains an independently structured factual summary with citation.

Exercise 1.28 reproduces two New York Times excerpts without an affirmative redistribution license. B003 excludes verbatim and translated expression while preserving independently structured factual study summaries, article citations, numbers, and inference questions.

The B003 scatterplot uses CIA World Factbook factual data. CIA site policy places unmarked CIA.gov information in the public domain and requests source credit; the derivative may include the localized derived plot with citation and without the CIA seal or any suggestion of endorsement.

The snowstorm caption carries a short Jon Stewart quotation without an affirmative reuse record. B003 replaces the direct translated expression with an independent climate-versus-weather paraphrase while retaining attribution.

The source defines a simple random sample through equal unit inclusion plus a claim of no association among selections. For fixed-size sampling without replacement the inclusion indicators are dependent, and equal marginal inclusion alone is insufficient. The derivative uses the defining equal probability for every possible sample of the fixed size.

The source says observational studies have two forms, prospective and retrospective, omitting cross-sectional and other designs. The derivative identifies these as two common forms discussed in this section.
The public answer names all births as the population but supports generalization only within Southern California. The derivative states a place-and-time-bounded Southern California target population.

The public answer claims broad population generalization solely because 200 participants were randomly sampled, although the exercise supplies no sampling frame. The derivative limits inference to the population represented by the unspecified frame.

The public answer treats similarity among sampled classes as sufficient for an unbiased multistage estimate. The derivative distinguishes precision from bias and identifies inclusion probabilities, weighting, and nonresponse as the relevant conditions.

Six source print-only page breaks or clears strand short continuations and leave severe underfill in the localized reader. B003 removes or locally suppresses only those break operations; all headings, prose, exercises, public answers, identifiers, multicolumn structure, figures, mathematics, and source order remain unchanged.

The derivative author strings omitted both middle-initial periods and the cedilla in Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel's PDF metadata. B003 restores David M. Diez, Mine Çetinkaya-Rundel, and Christopher D. Barr in visible attribution and metadata.

Whitespace around a zero-width index command renders a visible space before the period in the stratified-sampling caption. B003 moves the punctuation before the index command without changing the caption or index entry.

Two delayed footnote texts share hyperref's most recent destination state, leaving Hfootnote.6 absent and duplicating Hfootnote.7; the first marker consequently jumps to the cover. B003 emits each footnote text immediately after its own exercise marker, preserving text and numbering while restoring unique internal targets.

The source defines replication within a study as collecting a sufficiently large sample. Replication instead requires independent application of treatment conditions to multiple experimental units; repeating the entire study is a distinct additional form of replication. B004 states both precisely.

The source says randomization helps even out uncontrolled differences without stating the probabilistic limitation. B004 explains that measured and unmeasured differences balance in expectation and that one realized experiment is not guaranteed to have identical groups.

The source says the first three experimental-design principles should be incorporated into any study, although treatment assignment, randomization, and replication of treatment conditions are experimental principles. B004 limits the claim to experiments.

The source presents apparent improvement after placebo as an actual placebo effect without distinguishing natural history and other causes. B004 describes the observed response and explicitly states that it does not by itself prove placebo causation.

The source exercise treats post-randomization nonadherence as if it automatically introduced confounding. B004 preserves randomized assignment, explains that nonadherence complicates treatment-received estimation, and identifies the bias risk in an as-treated comparison.
The public answer omits the fluorescent lighting level named in exercise 1.31. B004 restores all three lighting levels while preserving the exercise-answer relation.

The public answer first fixes A as regular Coke and B as Diet Coke, then instructs the reader to randomize A and B, contradicting its own coding and weakening blinding. B004 randomly codes beverage identity for each trial, randomizes presentation order, and keeps participant and presenter blind until responses are recorded.

The authority producer assigns seeded control identities to box index 1 but draws index 1 in the lower box labeled Treatment, while treatment identities appear under Control. B004 corrects the y/threshold/reset mapping so exact seeded control and treatment IDs appear under the matching labels; the source-equivalence replay asserts every identity and coordinate.

The authority figure relies on unembedded ZapfDingbats glyphs for patient markers; those markers disappear in current Poppler rendering. B004 replaces them at source level with native vector open-circle and filled-triangle paths while preserving patient identities, risk classes, allocation, and alternative-text meaning.

The global exercise-header clear page left the end of Section 1.4 and the continuation of exercise 1.34 on severely underfilled pages. Under D013, B004 locally suppresses only that clear-page action while preserving the exercise heading, source order, all six exercises, labels, and public-answer relations.

The chapter include boundary and review-exercise header forced the short continuation of exercise 1.34 onto a page that remained about eighty percent empty before the Chapter 1 review exercises. Under D013, the completed localized Chapter 1 is input continuously and only the review header's clear-page action is suppressed; the chapter counter, heading, review exercises, source order, labels, and Chapter 2 boundary are preserved.

A print-only forced page break after exercise 1.41 left only its short continuation on an otherwise approximately eighty-five-percent empty page before exercise 1.42. Under D013, B004 removes only that break while preserving review exercises 1.35–1.44, labels, parts, source order, and the Chapter 2 boundary.

After removing forced breaks, the final part of exercise 1.44 still spilled naturally onto an otherwise empty page. B004 parameterizes the pre-existing 4 mm end-of-exercise gap and locally uses a readable 2.5 mm gap only for the ten Chapter 1 review exercises, reclaiming 15 mm without shrinking text, changing margins, or altering any exercise content, label, part, or order.

The mode discussion says that the histogram of loan_amount has one prominent peak, but the immediately preceding histogram and the example that follows are both explicitly about interest_rate. B005 changes only that variable reference to interest_rate.

The weighted-mean example refers to a county variable named income, which does not exist in the cited data and contradicts the surrounding per-capita-income calculation. B005 uses the existing per_capita_income identifier.

The robust-statistics opening marks interest_rate as a data set with the data macro even though it is a variable in loan50 and is marked as a variable everywhere around it. B005 changes only the semantic wrapper from data to var.

The box-plot alternative description begins with the malformed phrase 'What is shown in a a dot plot'. B005 supplies a complete natural Indonesian description while preserving every stated value and visual relation.

The table caption uses singular 'an extreme observations' and an awkward counterfactual construction. B005 renders the intended singular extreme observation and counterfactual comparison unambiguously.

The transformed-population scatterplot alternative description omits the verb in 'The data well distributed'. B005 restores the intended statement that the data are well distributed over the stated range without changing any numeric detail.
The mapping subsection contains subject-verb agreement errors in 'Figures ... shows' and 'One observation that stand out'. B005 corrects both while preserving the claims and references.

The skewness definition uses plural data with singular 'has' in 'When data trail off ... and has a longer right tail'. B005 renders the definition with consistent agreement and unchanged statistical meaning.
Exercise 1.43 spells Apache County as 'Apaice County' in three table rows. R011-B004R restores the correct Arizona county name without changing any table values.
Exercises 1.43(a) and 1.44(a) both ask which variables were collected 'in order to create to the summary table'. R011-B004R renders the intended question without the duplicated preposition.
Exercise 1.44(c) uses subject-verb disagreement in 'how the success rate of launches vary'. R011-B004R renders the intended statement with consistent agreement.

Public answer 1.43(a) classifies aggregate summary-table columns although exercise 1.43(a) asks which variables were collected for each traffic stop, while answer (b) says those individual variables are all categorical and non-ordinal. The derivative restores the five variables implied directly by the question, table, and unchanged parts (b)-(c): county, state, driver race, whether the vehicle was searched, and whether the driver was arrested.

The exercise alternative description says the scatterplot contains 62 points, copying the dataset row count, but only 55 cases have complete plotted coordinate pairs and the authority PDF content stream contains 55 point glyphs. B005 states the rendered count of 55 and replaces font-dependent point glyphs with 55 explicit vector circles for portable rendering.

The stacked-dot-plot alternative description lists 5 points at 11%, another 1 at 11%, and 3 at 12%; the official loan50 data and producer rounding instead yield 5 at 11%, 1 at 12%, and 3 at 13%. B005 corrects only those three stated positions.

The source caption says the bar plot summarizes the variable number, but the prose, data, axis, and figure all identify homeownership. B006 corrects only the caption variable reference to homeownership.

In the first-panel alternative description, the source swaps the color/category mapping for the rent bar: blue is described as joint near 3,500 and yellow as individual near 400, contrary to the data, the other panels, and the next sentence. B006 restores blue as individual and yellow as joint without changing the plotted values.

The source public footnote answer gives group medians of about $45,000 and $40,000, while the source figure median lines and its own alternative description show approximately $53,000 for Gain and $45,000 for No Gain. B006 uses the figure-supported values 53,000 and 45,000; no data or graphic geometry is changed.

The source public answer names the categories Yes, No, and Not Sure, while the exercise and figure use Support, Not Support, and Not Sure. B006 aligns the answer with the final localized figure labels Mendukung, Tidak mendukung, and Tidak yakin.
The source alternative description misspells the plotted category Neuromuscular as Neuromascular. B006 renders the intended category name Neuromuscular.
